component.name: com.unity.usd-toolkit
component.description: Runtime USD toolkit for Unity applications using a custom native OpenUSD wrapper. A C# integration layer for connecting Unity to NVIDIA's Omniverse/OpenUSD ecosystem. Wraps Pixar's OpenUSD 26.05 native binaries via P/Invoke so Unity can read, write, and round-trip USD stages.

properties.name: unity:provenanceNote
properties.value: Every OpenUSD payload is built from the public v26.05 tag (commit 2095faf) with one Unity patch applied (recorded in the OpenUSD component's pedigree) and the flags recorded on that component. MaterialX 1.39.4 is built by the same build_usd.py run from the upstream source archive whose SHA-256 is pinned on the MaterialX source component; that archive, like every pinned archive, is verified before build_usd.py runs and again after it finishes. The builds are not bit-reproducible: no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, absolute build paths are embedded, and the macOS payload is post-processed with install_name_tool and codesign. The SHA-256 values here identify what shipped; they do not prove upstream authenticity.

components.name: OpenUSD
components.description: The source every shipped OpenUSD payload is built from: public tag v26.05, commit 2095faf ("Merge release v26.05"), with the Unity patches in this component's pedigree applied, monolithic, the same flags on every platform.

resolves.name: LZ4 1.9.2 memmove() with a negative size; OpenUSD's crate reader could pass an output size above INT_MAX
TfFastCompression::DecompressFromBuffer did not check chunk count or chunk sizes read from the file against the buffer
usdDraco wrote past its value buffers and read outside its face table on indices and strides read from the file, and crashed on meshes UsdDraco_WriteDraco itself wrote
usdAbc dereferenced the null samples Alembic returns under kQuietNoopPolicy for data it cannot read

The crate (.usdc) reader allocated, and value-initialized, for array, table, list and dictionary counts read from the file before checking them against it, so a damaged file could exhaust memory, and kept compressed integer arrays whose data was short, decoded from uninitialized memory
Damaged path jumps made the crate reader spawn tasks without bound and write one path from several threads, and deeply nested values overflowed the stack
The crate reader took table-of-contents section ranges outside the file and unterminated section names unchecked, and time samples with more times than values read other data as their values
OpenUSD refused the Draco plugin in any monolithic Windows build, for missing symbols only its Python module needs; allowed without Python
usdDraco's writer (UsdDraco_WriteDraco) exported from the OpenUSD library, so .drc files can be written
TBB's version banner, built into the macOS and Linux TBB libraries, named the machine that built them

components.description: Vendored inside OpenUSD as pxr/base/tf/pxrTslRobinMap. The vendored copy declares no version; it is whatever OpenUSD v26.05 ships.

components.name: libdeflate
components.description: Vendored inside OpenUSD as pxr/imaging/plugin/hioOpenEXR/OpenEXR/deflate, but in no OpenUSD binary: hioOpenEXR is not built under --no-imaging. Its decompressor is compiled into the wrapper (Native~/src/UsdDeflate.c) as the inflate the image codecs use on every platform; Native~/CMakeLists.txt checks the 29 files against recorded digests.

components.name: MaterialX
components.description: The source every shipped MaterialX library is built from: the upstream v1.39.4 archive, pinned by SHA-256 and verified before and after build_usd.py, built by that run with render back-ends off.

components.name: pugixml
components.description: Vendored inside MaterialX as source/MaterialXFormat/External/PugiXML and compiled into libMaterialXFormat (PUGIXML_VERSION 190). Its MIT notice is at the end of that pugixml.hpp.

components.name: MaterialX data libraries
components.description: The MaterialX standard data libraries (stdlib, pbrlib, bxdf, cmlib, lights, nprlib, targets: .mtlx definitions and GLSL/MSL/OSL/MDL shader source) that build_usd.py installs for usdMtlx, from the same MaterialX build. Mostly "Contributors to the MaterialX Project" under Apache-2.0; the mdl/materialx files are NVIDIA CORPORATION, Apache-2.0; stdlib/genglsl/lib/mx_noise.glsl and mx_hsv.glsl, the stdlib/genosl/include headers and part of mdl/materialx/noise.mdl are derived from Open Shading Language (Sony Pictures Imageworks / Contributors to the OSL project), BSD-3-Clause. unity:treeSha256 is the SHA-256 of sorted `shasum -a 256` lines over the tree, .meta files excluded.

components.name: Alembic
components.description: Alembic, built static (Ogawa only, no HDF5) and linked into the monolithic OpenUSD library by usdAbc, the plugin that reads and writes .abc files, with the Unity patch in this component's pedigree applied.

resolves.name: Ogawa reader copied a data block into a buffer sized by a separate, unchecked dimensions block (heap overflow), and dereferenced null data and samples

components.name: Imath
components.description: Imath, the vector and half-float types Alembic uses, built static by OpenEXR's build from the pinned archive (FetchContent pointed at it, downloads disconnected) and linked into the monolithic OpenUSD library with Alembic.

components.name: OpenEXR
components.description: Compiled by build_usd.py only because it builds Alembic's Imath through OpenEXR. None of its libraries is linked into any shipped file.

components.name: Draco
components.description: Draco, built static and linked into the monolithic OpenUSD library by usdDraco, the plugin that reads .drc meshes. Its third_party directory (eigen, filesystem, googletest, tinygltf) serves the tests and the glTF transcoder, which are not built.
